analysis.text: 开场介绍嘉宾的直接陈述。主持人开场介绍嘉宾时直接给出身份 a three-time Olympic champion and author，这是访谈交代人物的固定位置，无需转折提示，听到头衔即定位。

questions.stem: What is the woman's book mainly about?

questions.answerText: How technology has helped athletes to scale new heights.

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问书名含义时的总括应答。主持人请她解释书名，她答 The book is about how…—— The book is about 是直接给主旨的总括句，正是被问者对『书讲什么』的应答落点。

analysis.text: I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge. 我认为，几千年来我们的身体并没有改变，真正改变的是科学知识。

analysis.text: while 引导的『没变 vs 变了』对比。while our bodies have not changed 与 what has changed is the scientific knowledge 形成正反对比，while 是让步对比信号；题问『变了 什么』，落点在对比里『变了』的那一侧。

analysis.text: what has changed is the scientific knowledge ↔Our scientific knowledge. 原句明点 scientific knowledge=选项几乎原词

analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 原文说 our bodies have not changed，身体属于『没变』的一侧；Our physical structures. 正是身体结构，恰好答反——题问的是『变了』的，它却是『没变』的。 借用原文：our bodies have not changed in thousands of years C) 原词陷阱 Our biochemical process. 借原文 human biochemistry 设套；biochemistry 只是『知 识』所含的内容之一，原文明说变的是 scientific knowledge，不是某个生化过程本身。 借用原文：our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics D) 原词陷阱 Our concept of nutrition. 借原文 nutrition 一词诱选；营养同样只是知识涵盖的内容之 一，并非原文点名『变了』的那一项。 借用原文：human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics

questions.stem: What is the man's concern about the use of technology in sports competitions?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士对在体育比赛中使用技术有什么担忧?
questions.answerText: It may give an unfair advantage to some athletes.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others? 会不会有这样的担忧：技术正在让某些运动员相比其他人获得不公平的优势？

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: concern 一词直接标示担忧+由男士问出。男士的问句以 Is there any concern that… 直接 打出 concern 信号，且本题问『男士的担忧』，落点正在他这句问话，而非女士的回答。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others ↔ It may give an unfair advantage to some athletes 近原句重述，仅时态/语序微调

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 It may increase the expenses of sports competitions. 谈比赛开支，全篇没有任何关于 花钱/成本的内容，纯属凭空添加。 B) 过度推断 女士回答里提到 Skis 这类装备，易诱人推出 It may lead to athletes' over-reliance on equipment.；但原文谈滑雪板是讲技术进步，从未说运动员『过度依赖装备』，是凭装备 话题硬推的隐患。 借用原文：Skis, for example, went from being made of wood to a metal alloy D) 过度推断 It may change the nature of sports competitions. 说法宏大，像是对 unfair advantage 的拔高引申；但男士担忧的是『公平』这一具体点，原文从未说科技会『改变比赛本质』。 1 W: I've worked in international trade all my life. My father did so too before me. So I guess you could say it runs in the family. W: 我一辈子都在做国际贸易。我父亲在我之前也是做这个的。所以我想你可以说这是家族传承吧。 2 M: What products have you worked with? M: 你都做过哪些产品？ 3 W: All sorts, really. I've imported textiles, machinery, toys, solar panels, all kinds of things over the years. Trends and demand come and go. So one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry. W: 真的是各种各样的。这些年来我进口过纺织品、机械、玩具、太阳能电池板，什么都有。潮流和需求 都是来来去去的。所以在这个行业要成功就得非常灵活。 4 M: I see. What goods are you trading now? M: 明白了。你现在在做什么商品？ 5 W: I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China. I even use the same container. It's a very efficient way of conducting trade. W: 我现在从中国进口家具到意大利，从意大利进口食品到中国。我甚至用同一个集装箱。这是一种非常 高效的贸易方式。 6 M: The same container? You mean you own a 40-foot cargo container? M: 同一个集装箱？你是说你有一个40英尺的货柜？ 7 W: Yeah. that's right. I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai. I source mid- century modern furniture from different factories in China. It's very good value for money. I collect it all in my warehouse and then dispatch it to my other warehouse in Italy. Over there I do the same, but with Italian foods instead of furniture, things like pasta, cheese, wine, chocolates. And I send all that to my warehouse in China in the same freight container I use for the furniture. W: 对，没错。我在意大利Genova有一个仓库，在上海还有一个。我从中国不同的工厂采购中世纪现代风 格的家具。性价比非常高。我把所有东西集中在我的仓库里，然后发到我在意大利的另一个仓库。在那边 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 我做同样的事，但是换成意大利食品而不是家具，比如意大利面、奶酪、红酒、巧克力。然后我用运家具 的那个货柜把这些全都运到我在中国的仓库。 8 M: So I presume you sell both lines of products wholesale in each respective country. M: 那我猜你在各自的国家都是批发这两类产品。 9 W: Of course. I possess a network of clients and partners in both countries. That's the main benefit of having done this for so long. I've made great business contacts over time. W: 当然。我在两个国家都有客户和合作伙伴网络。这就是做这行这么久的主要好处。我积累了很好的商 业关系。 10 M: How many times do you ship? M: 你一年运多少次？ 11 W: I did 12 shipments last year, 18 this year, and I hope to grow to around 25 next year. That's both ways, there and back again. Demand for authentic Italian food in China is growing rapidly. And similarly, sales of affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture are also increasing in Italy. Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties. W: 去年我运了12次，今年18次，我希望明年能增长到25次左右。这是双向的，来回都算。中国对正宗意 大利食品的需求增长很快。同样，意大利对实惠又时尚的木质家具的销量也在增长。家具的利润稍微高一 点，主要是因为关税更低。

questions.stem: What does the woman think is required to be successful in international trade?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士认为在国际贸易中取得成功需要什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Trends and demand come and go. So one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry. 潮流和需求来来去去。所以要在这一行成功，人就必须非常灵活。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: needs to be… to succeed 的"必需"句式。答案信号是表"必需"的句式 one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry——needs to be… 直接点出成功所必须具备的 那一项，正是 Q5"required to be successful"对应的落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: one needs to be very flexible ↔Flexibility. 形容词 flexible 转名词 Flexibility

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Experience. 是凭常识"显然要有"的项，但录音从没说成功"需要"经验；她只在讲资历时旁 及做了一辈子，并未把经验列为"required to be successful"。 C) 原词陷阱 Family background. 听着像录音里 it runs in the family(这行在家里传承)，于是"听到家庭 就想选"；但那句只是介绍她的出身经历，回答的是"她怎么入行"，并非"成功所必需"，与 Q5 问的不是一回事。 借用原文：it runs in the family D) 原词陷阱 Business connections. 对应录音后文 I've made great business contacts over time，但 她把人脉说成"做久了的好处"(benefit)，是结果不是"成功的必需条件"；且这话出现在 Q7 附近，搬到 Q5 来答属张冠李戴。 借用原文：I've made great business contacts over time

questions.stem: What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说她的贸易方式有什么特别之处?
questions.answerText: Using the same container back and forth.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China. I even use the same container. It's a very efficient way of conducting trade. 我现在把家具从中国进口到意大利，把食品从意大利进口到中国。我甚至用同一个集装箱。 这是一种非常高效的贸易方式。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: even 的强调语气 + "非常高效"评价。答案信号是强调词 I even use the same container 里的 even(甚至)，加上紧跟的 It's a very efficient way 自评"非常高效"——even 把这个做 法特意拎出来当作不寻常之处，正是 Q6 的"special"。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I even use the same container ↔Using the same container back and forth. "用同一集装箱"概括为"往返复用"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Buying directly from factories. 听着像录音 I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories，于是"听到工厂就想选"；但从工厂进货是常规做法、她也没说这 点特别，与 Q6 问的"special"不符。 借用原文：from different factories in China B) 未提及 Shipping goods in bulk by sea. 是外贸最普通的做法，听着合理，但录音通篇没说"海 运"或"大宗"，属凭常识脑补、原文未提。 C) 原词陷阱 Having partners in many parts of the world. 借用了录音 I possess a network of clients and partners 的"伙伴"原词，但录音说的合作伙伴只在 in both countries(两国)， 选项却扩成 many parts of the world(世界许多地方)，范围被放大且这是 Q7 附近的内 容，搬来答 Q6 也不对路。 借用原文：partners in both countries

questions.stem: What does the woman have in both Italy and China?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士在意大利和中国都拥有什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai. 我在意大利的热那亚有一个仓库，在上海还有另一个。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: I have… and another in… 的两地并列。答案信号是"两地各有一个"的并列句式 I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai——a warehouse… and another… 明确说出两国各有一个仓库，正对 Q7 的"in both Italy and China"。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai ↔Warehouses. 单数 a warehouse + another 合为复数

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 Factories. 盗用录音 from different factories in China 的高频原词，"听到工厂就想选"； 但工厂是她进货的对象、属于别人，并非她在两地都"拥有"的东西，与 Q7 的 have 不符。 借用原文：from different factories in China C) 未提及Investors. 全篇没有出现，录音里没有任何关于投资人的内容，纯属未提及。 D) 与原文相反 Retailers.(零售商)与录音相反：M 说她 sell both lines of products wholesale(批发销 售)、她答 Of course，说明走的是批发渠道，不是零售；且她"拥有"的是仓库，不是零售 商。 借用原文：sell both lines of products wholesale

questions.stem: What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说什么使家具的利润略微提高?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties. 家具的利润略微高一些，主要是因为它享有较低的关税。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: mostly because 的因果信号。答案信号是因果连词 mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties 里的 because——它直接引出"利润略高"的原因，正是 Q8 要的归因 落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: lower customs duties ↔Lower import duties. customs duties = import duties 同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Trendy style. 听着像录音 affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture 的 stylish，于是"听到 时髦就想选"；但那句讲的是家具在意大利"销量增长"(好卖)，不是"利润略高的原因"，把"好 卖"当成了"更赚钱"。 借用原文：affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture B) 未提及 Unique design. 与 A 同属"产品卖点"类，但录音根本没说家具"设计独特"，更没把它当作 利润高的原因，属未提及。 D) 偷换概念 Lower shipping costs.(更低运费)与 C 极易混，但录音明说原因是 lower customs duties(关税)，从未把利润高归于运费；shipping 一词虽在别处出现，这里却答非所问。 借用原文：lower customs duties Section B 1 "Too many people view their jobs as a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday," says Joel Goodman, founder of the Humour Project, a humour consulting group in Saratoga Springs, New York. Humour unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job. "太多人把自己的工作视为一座为期五天的监狱,每周五才能获得假释,"Joel Goodman说道,他是Humour Project的创始人,这是一家位于纽约萨拉托加斯普林斯的幽默咨询公司。幽默能打开办公室的牢笼,因为它 让成年人能够将一些童真精神带入工作中。 2 According to Howard Pollio, professor of psychology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, an office with humour breaks is an office with satisfied and productive employees. Pollio conducted a study that proved humour can help workers excel at routine production tasks. Employees perform better when they have fun. 田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校的心理学教授Howard Pollio认为,一个有幽默休息时间的办公室就是一个员工 满意且富有成效的办公室。Pollio进行了一项研究,证明幽默可以帮助员工在日常生产任务中表现出色。当 员工感到快乐时,他们的表现会更好。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 In large corporations with a hierarchy of power, there is often no outlet for stress. "Every company needs underground ways of poking fun at the organization," says Lynn N. Mark, a speaker on workplace humour for St. Mary's Health Centre in St. Louis. 在有权力等级制度的大型企业中,往往没有释放压力的出口。"每家公司都需要一些地下方式来调侃组 织,"Lynn N. Mark说道,她是圣路易斯St. Mary's Health Centre的职场幽默演讲者。 4 Kodak's Rochester, New York branch discovered a way for its 20,000 employees to uncork their bottled-up resentments. Their 1,000-square-foot Humour Room features a toy store. Among the room's many stress-reducing gadgets, the main attraction is a boss doll with detachable arms and legs. Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place. Kodak位于纽约罗切斯特的分公司为其两万名员工找到了一种释放积压怨气的方法。他们面积一千平方英 尺的幽默室设有一个玩具商店。在该房间众多的减压小工具中,最吸引人的是一个可拆卸手臂和腿的老板玩 偶。员工可以把玩偶拆开,只要他们把手臂和腿放回原位即可。 5 Sandy Cohen, owner of a graphic print production business, created the Quote Board to document the bizarre phrases people say when under strict deadlines. "When you're under stress, you say stupid things," says Cohen. "Now we just look at each other and say, that's one for the Quote Board." 平面印刷制作公司老板Sandy Cohen创建了语录板,用来记录人们在严格期限压力下说出的奇怪话语。"当 你处于压力之下时,你会说些蠢话,"Cohen说。"现在我们只是互相看看对方,然后说,这句话该上语录 板了。"

questions.answerText: It helps employees to reduce their stress.

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开篇点题句 + 后文减压主线。首段把职场比作 a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday（把工作日比作要熬到周五才获释的监狱），紧接一句 Humour unlocks the office prison——开篇用"幽默解开办公室监狱"点题；其后各段（P3 谈 outlet for stress、P4 谈 uncork their bottled-up resentments）持续指向缓解压力，主 旨主线就是"减压"。

questions.stem: What can Kodak's employees do in the Humour Room?
questions.stemZh: Kodak的员工在幽默室可以做什么?
questions.answerText: Take the boss doll apart as long as they reassemble it.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place. 只要把玩偶的胳膊和腿装回原位，员工就可以把它拆开。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 条件状语 as long as 是落点。答案句的灵魂在 as long as they put its arms and legs back in place——as long as（只要……）是个条件限定，告诉你"可以拆，但前提是装回 去"；听力里这种条件/限定词后面往往就是出题的精确落点，必须听全。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: take the doll apart ↔Take the boss doll apart 拆开动作对应 as long as they put its arms and legs back in place ↔as long as they reassemble it 装回=重新组装

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Smash the toys to release their bottled-up resentments. 把 P4 的 toy store 与 P4 的 uncork their bottled-up resentments 两处原词拼在一起，但录音说的是"拆开（take apart）并装回"，绝非"砸碎（smash）"，动作被改狠了。 借用原文：uncork their bottled-up resentments C) 原词陷阱 Design and install stress-reducing gadgets. 借了原文 stress-reducing gadgets 一词， 但录音说这些装置是房间里现成的陈设（the room's many stress-reducing gadgets）， 员工是去用、不是去"设计安装（design and install）"，把现成品说成员工自造，动作主体 与行为都错位。 借用原文：the room's many stress-reducing gadgets D) 与原文相反 Strike at the boss doll as hard as they like. 围着真实存在的 boss doll，且 as hard as they like（想多狠就多狠）很诱人，但录音明确是 take apart（拆开）且必须 put arms and legs back in place（装回），既不是"使劲打"，更没有"随心所欲、无须复原"——条 件被抹掉了。 借用原文：as long as they put its arms and legs back in place 1 Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. The news was made known by Rockefeller University geneticist Jeffrey Friedman. The researchers believe this gene influences development of a hormone that tells the organism how fat or full it is. Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can't tell when to stop eating. 最近在肥胖小鼠身上发现的一个变异基因引起了公众的兴趣。这一消息由洛克菲勒大学遗传学家Jeffrey Friedman公布。研究人员认为这个基因影响一种激素的发育,这种激素会告诉机体自身有多胖或多饱。那 些携带变异基因的个体可能无法感知自己是否已经吃够或是否有足够的脂肪组织,因此无法知道何时停止 进食。 2 The researchers also reported finding a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans. The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated, however. Still, professionals like University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum reacted enthusiastically: "This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height." 研究人员还报告称在人类身上发现了一个与小鼠肥胖基因几乎相同的基因。然而,这个基因在人类体内的作 用尚未得到证实。尽管如此,像佛蒙特大学心理学家Esther Rothblum这样的专业人士仍反应热烈:"这项研 究表明,人们确实天生就有保持某种体重的倾向,就像他们天生具有特定的肤色或身高一样。" 3 Actually, behavioral geneticists believe that less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes, while height is almost entirely genetically determined. 实际上,行为遗传学家认为,总体重变异中只有不到一半是由基因决定的,而身高几乎完全由基因决定。 Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard. 4 Whatever role genes play, Americans are getting fatter. A survey by the Center for Disease Control found that obesity has increased greatly over the last 10 years. Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods, in Americans' overeating. 无论基因起什么作用,美国人正在变得越来越胖。疾病控制中心的一项调查发现,在过去10年中肥胖症大幅 增加。这种快速变化凸显了环境因素的作用,比如丰富食物的充裕导致美国人饮食过量。 5 The Center for Disease Control has also found that teens are far less physically active than they were even a decade ago. Accepting that weight is predetermined can relieve guilt for overweight people. But people's belief that they cannot control their weight can itself contribute to obesity. 疾病控制中心还发现,青少年的体育活动量远低于十年前。接受体重是预先决定的这一观点可以减轻超重人 群的负罪感。但是,人们相信自己无法控制体重这一信念本身就可能导致肥胖。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say has aroused public interest?

analysis.text: Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. 公众的兴趣是被肥胖小鼠体内一个发生改变的基因这一最新发现所引起的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 题干原词 aroused 对应开篇句。篇章开头第一句 Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. 直接出现题干里的 aroused 与 public interest，开篇点题句就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice ↔ The recent finding of a changed gene in obese mice. latest=recent、discovery=finding

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 过度推断 录音只说发现了一个改变的基因，从未称其为 A breakthrough in understanding gene modification.；breakthrough 与 gene modification 都是原文没有的拔高说法，把一次 发现夸成理解上的突破，推过了头。 C) 偷换概念 A newly discovered way for people to lose weight. 借用了原文 discovery 的味道，却 把对象从小鼠的基因偷换成给人减肥的方法；原文 a changed gene in obese mice 讲的是 小鼠基因，根本没说找到了减肥办法。 借用原文：the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice D) 原词陷阱 The self-repairing ability of a gene in obese mice. 借了 gene 与 obese mice 这些原 词，但原文从未提到基因有自我修复能力，self-repairing 是凭空捏造的内容。 借用原文：a changed gene in obese mice

questions.stem: What do we learn about the changed gene?
questions.stemZh: 关于这个改变的基因我们了解到什么?
questions.answerText: It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can't tell when to stop eating. 带有这个变化基因的个体，可能感知不到自己何时已吃饱、或脂肪组织是否已足够，因而无 法判断该何时停止进食。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果 thus 引出后果。句中 and thus can't tell when to stop eating 用 thus 把基因的后 果点出来——感知不到饱、判断不了何时停吃，正是题干要的那个作用，因果信号词之后即 答案落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: can't tell when to stop eating ↔It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating. can't tell=unable to sense

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 It renders an organism unable to fight diseases. 借了原文出现过的 organism 一词，但 原文只说基因影响对饱腹的感知，从未提到它让生物无法抗病，fight diseases 是没说过的 内容。 借用原文：tells the organism how fat or full it is B) 与原文相反 It prevents the mice's fatty tissues from growing. 盗用了原文的 fatty tissue，却把意思 反了——原文说的是带该基因者感知不到脂肪是否够 if they have sufficient fatty tissue， 并非这个基因会阻止脂肪生长。 借用原文：if they have sufficient fatty tissue C) 未提及 It helps organisms adapt to environmental changes. 又一次借用 organism，但帮助适 应环境的说法原文完全没有，是凭空加上的功能。 借用原文：tells the organism how fat or full it is

questions.stem: What does University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum say?
questions.stemZh: Vermont大学心理学家Esther Rothblum说了什么?
questions.answerText: People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: "This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height." “这项研究表明，人确实生来就有形成某种体重的倾向，就像他们生来就有特定的肤色或身 高一样。”

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 人物引述原话。原文 reacted enthusiastically: 之后是 Rothblum 的直接引语，引号内 people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight 即她的观点，被引述 人原话就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight ↔ People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight. 近乎原句保留

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Human beings have more obesity genes than most mice do. 借了原文人与鼠都有相近 基因的话题，但 Rothblum 从没比较人和鼠谁的肥胖基因更多，这一数量对比原文没有。 借用原文：a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans B) 张冠李戴 Half of a person's total weight variation can be controlled. 把第三段行为遗传学家说的 less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes 安到了 Rothblum 头上，既换了说话人，又把不到一半由基因决定篡改成半数可控。 借用原文：less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes D) 张冠李戴 The function of the obesity genes is yet to be explored. 对应的是原文 The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated，那是叙述者的客观补充，并非 Rothblum 的话，被错挂到她名下。 借用原文：The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated

options.label: A

options.label: B

questions.stem: What accounts for Americans' obesity according to a survey by the Center for Disease Control?
questions.stemZh: 根据疾病控制中心的一项调查,美国人的肥胖归因于什么?
questions.answerText: The abundant provision of rich foods.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods, in Americans' overeating. 如此迅速的变化凸显了环境因素——比如丰富的高热量食物——在美国人暴饮暴食中所起的 作用。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: underlines the role 点明成因。原文 Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods 用 underlines the role of 这 一归因表达点出主因是环境因素，并举 rich foods 为例，正是题干要的原因。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the abundance of rich foods ↔The abundant provision of rich foods. abundance=abundant provision

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 The worsening of natural environment. 蹭了原文 environmental factors 里的 environmental，却把环境因素偷换成自然环境恶化；原文说的环境因素指的是食物丰富等 生活环境，并非自然环境变差。 借用原文：the role of environmental factors C) 未提及 The accelerated pace of present-day life. 听着合理，但这项调查归因到的是丰富食物， 原文从未把肥胖归因于生活节奏加快，pace of life 是没说过的因素。 D) 偷换概念 The adverse impact of the food industry. 借食物话题制造与 B 的混淆，但原文归因的是 the abundance of rich foods（丰富食物本身），并没把责任算到食品工业头上，food industry 是替换上去的对象。 借用原文：the abundance of rich foods Section C 1 Qualities of a relationship, such as openness, compassion, and mental stimulation are of concern to most of us regardless of sex, but—judging from the questionnaire response—they are more important to women than to men. 关系的品质,如开放性、同情心和精神刺激,是我们大多数人关注的问题,无论性别如何,但从问卷调查的回应 来看,这些品质对女性比对男性更重要。 2 Asked to consider the ingredients of close friendship, women rated these qualities above all others. Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% male respondents. Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men as well as women, was the only area of overlap. Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality; caring was picked by just 23%. 当被要求考虑亲密友谊的要素时,女性将这些品质排在所有其他品质之上。男性给予它们较低的优先级,而 更青睐兴趣相似性(77%的男性选择)和危机中的响应能力(61%的男性受访者选择)。精神刺激在男性和女 性中都排名第三,是唯一重叠的领域。在男性中,只有28%的人将开放性列为重要品质;关怀仅被23%的人 选择。 3 It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships they are referring to emotional factors, while men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company. That is, when a man speaks of "a friend" he is likely to be talking about someone he does things with—a teammate, a Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. fellow hobbyist, a drinking buddy. These activities are the fabric of the friendship; it is a "doing" relationship in which similarity in interests is the key bond. This factor was a consideration of less than 11% of women. Women opt for a warm, emotional atmosphere where communication flows freely; activity is mere background. 从他们的选择中可以明显看出,当女性谈论亲密友谊时,她们指的是情感因素,而男性强调的是他们在朋友陪 伴中找到的快乐。也就是说,当一个男人谈论"朋友"时,他很可能是在谈论与他一起做事的人——队友、同 好者、酒友。这些活动是友谊的织体;这是一种"行动"关系,其中兴趣相似性是关键纽带。这一因素只有不 到11%的女性考虑。女性选择温暖的情感氛围,在那里交流自由流动;活动只是背景。 4 Lastly, men, as we have seen, have serious questions about each other's loyalty. Perhaps this is why they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis—"someone I can call on for help." Women, as their testimonies indicate, are generally more secure with each other and consequently are more likely to treat this issue lightly. In follow-up interviews this was confirmed numerous times as woman after woman indicated that "being there when needed was taken for granted." 最后,正如我们所见,男性对彼此的忠诚度有严重的疑问。也许这就是为什么他们如此强调危机中的响应能 力——"我可以求助的人"。女性,正如她们的证言所示,彼此之间通常更有安全感,因此更可能轻视这个问 题。在后续访谈中,这一点得到了多次证实,一位又一位女性表示"在需要时在场是理所当然的"。 5 As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cutthroat competition and feelings of betrayal. This applies to both men and women, but unequally. In comparison, nearly twice as many men complained about these issues as women. Further, while competition and betrayal are the main thorns to female friendship, men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly. analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Failure to keep a promise. 听上去合理，但录音讲隐患时只点了 competition、 betrayal、lack of frankness、fear of appearing unmanly，从未提"违背承诺"，属未提 及。 B) 原词陷阱 Lack of frankness. 录音确实念到，但 men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness 说这是"额外"困扰男性的问题，并非男女双方共 有，与题干 both 不符，是原词陷阱。 借用原文：men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly D) 未提及 Loss of contact. 是最符合常识的"友谊杀手"，但录音整段讲隐患从未提及"失联"，正是预 读时警惕的那个常识诱饵。 1 The partial skeletons of more than 20 dinosaurs and the scattered bones of about 300 more have been discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument. Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada. This dinosaur pit is the largest and best preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today. 在现今的恐龙国家纪念地，于犹他州和科罗拉多州发现了20多具恐龙的部分骨架以及大约300具恐龙的零 散骨骼。许多最佳标本今天可以在美国和加拿大较大城市的自然历史博物馆中看到。这个恐龙化石坑是当 今已知最大且保存最完好的恐龙化石沉积地。 2 Many people get the idea from the mass of bones in the pit wall that some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area. This could have happened but it probably did not. 许多人从坑壁上大量的骨骼得出这样的想法：某种灾难，如火山爆发或突发洪水，在这一地区杀死了整群 恐龙。这种情况可能发生过，但很可能并非如此。 3 The main reasons for thinking otherwise are the scattered bones and the thickness of the deposit. 认为并非如此的主要原因是零散的骨骼和沉积层的厚度。 4 In other deposits where the animals were thought to have died together, the skeletons were usually complete and often all the bones were in their proper places. Rounded pieces of fossil bone have been found here. These fragments got their smooth round shape by rolling along the stream bottom. 在其他被认为动物一起死亡的沉积地中，骨架通常是完整的，而且所有骨骼往往都处于它们应有的位置。 这里发现了圆润的化石骨骼碎片。这些碎片通过沿着河床滚动而形成了光滑的圆形形状。 Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. 5 In a mass killing, the bones would have been left on the stream or lake bottom together at the same level. But in this deposit, the bones occur throughout a zone of sandstone about 12 feet thick. 在集体死亡事件中，骨骼应该一起留在河流或湖底的同一水平面上。但在这个沉积层中，骨骼分布在大约 12英尺厚的砂岩层中。 6 The mixture of swamp dwellers and dry-land types also seems to indicate that the deposit is a mixture from different places. 沼泽居住类型和干旱陆地类型的混合似乎也表明该沉积层是来自不同地方的混合物。 7 The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died. Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar. Some of them may have come from far-away dry-land areas to the west. Perhaps they drowned trying to cross a small stream or were washed away during floods. Some of the swamp dwellers may have got stuck in the very sandbar that became their grave; others may have floated for miles before being stranded. 这个化石坑区域是一个大型恐龙墓地，而不是它们死亡的地方。大部分遗骸可能顺着向东流淌的河流漂 流，直到被留在浅沙洲上。其中一些可能来自遥远的西部干旱陆地区域。也许它们在试图穿越小溪时溺水 身亡，或在洪水期间被冲走。一些沼泽居住者可能被困在成为它们坟墓的沙洲上；另一些可能漂流了数英 里后才搁浅。 8 Even today similar events take place. When floods come in the spring, sheep, cattle and deer are often trapped by rising waters and often drown. Their dead bodies float downstream until the flood recedes and leaves them stranded on a bar or shore where they lie, half buried in the sand, until they decay. Early travelers on the Missouri river reported that shores and bars were often lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods. 即使在今天，类似的事件仍在发生。当春季洪水来临时，绵羊、牛和鹿经常被上涨的洪水困住并溺死。它 们的尸体顺流而下漂流，直到洪水退去，将它们搁浅在沙洲或岸边，半埋在沙中，直到腐烂。早期在密苏 里河上旅行的人报告说，河岸和沙洲上经常堆满了在春季洪水中死亡的野牛腐烂的尸体。

And this is true. But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy. So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent. 这个国家的年轻人被指责不像在原籍国那样照顾父母。这是事实。但同样真实的是,老年人也受到了美国独 立和自主理想的影响。所以我们独自生活,也许在饥饿的边缘,最终没有朋友,但我们是独立的。 3 This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group, although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical. It is a poor ideal and pursuing it does a great deal of harm. This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness. 这种标准的美国式生活方式被强加在每个族裔群体身上,尽管对许多群体来说这种理想并不实用。这是一个 糟糕的理想,追求它会造成很大的伤害。这种独立的理想也包含着大量的无私。 Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. 4 In talking to today's young mothers. I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they are going to be. I hear devoted, loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers. They are astonished to hear that in most of the world throughout most of its history, families have been three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof. 在与当今年轻母亲交谈时,我问她们认为自己将成为什么样的祖母。我听到充满爱心的母亲说,当她们抚养 完孩子后,她们无意成为祖母。她们惊讶地听到,在世界大部分地区的大部分历史中,家庭一直是三代或四代 同堂的家庭,住在同一屋檐下。 5 We have over-emphasized the small family unit—father, mother, small children. We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they're still alive, can live alone. We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way and the only thing we can do for our daughter-in-law is to see as little of her as possible. 我们过分强调了小家庭单元——父亲、母亲、年幼的孩子。我们认为如果祖父母还在世,能够独自生活是 很美好的。我们已经到了这样的地步:我们认为我们能为孩子做的唯一的事就是不妨碍他们,我们能为儿媳 做的唯一的事就是尽可能少见她。 6 Old people's nursing homes, even the best run, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit. So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to "not being a burden". 老人疗养院,即使是管理最好的,也住满了这样的老人:他们相信自己能为孩子做的唯一的事就是在孩子来探 望时表现得高高兴兴。所以最终,老年人不得不把所有精力都投入到"不成为负担"上。 7 We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy. We've isolated old people and we've cut off the children from their grandparents. 我们开始看到,为了强调独立和自主,我们付出了多么巨大的代价。我们孤立了老年人,我们切断了孩子与祖 父母的联系。 8 One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out. Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most—perspective, to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do. 我们今天的代沟如此严重的原因之一,就是祖父母退出了。年轻人被剥夺了他们最需要的东西——视角,去 了解为什么他们的父母行为如此古怪,为什么他们的祖父母说那些话。

analysis.text: And, ironic as it sounds, since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now reproduce beyond the environment's carrying capacity. 而且，听起来虽然讽刺：既然人类已经消灭了许多动物天敌，有人就把狩猎看作一种天然手 段，用来削减那些如今繁殖数量已超过环境承载力的猎物种群。 51. What does the author say sounds ironic? A) Some predators may often turn out to be prey of other predators. B) Hunting may also be a solution to the problem caused by hunting. questions.stem: What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干 What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees? 索取一个具名人物 对一个具体做法的明确观点，原文必有对应表述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees? 中 charging hunters license fees 是动名词短语作 of 的宾语，charge sb. sth. 即"向某人收取某费"。基础薄弱 考生易把 charging 误读为现在分词"正在收费的"，要看清它是名词性结构。 52. What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees? A) It keeps game population under control. B) It turns hunting into a sport of the rich. C) It leads to ecological imbalance. D) It helps stop killing for pleasure.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: He adds that, despite hunters' claims that hunting keeps wildlife populations in balance, hunters' license fees are used to "manipulate a few game species into overpopulation at the expense of a much larger number of non-game species, resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance." 他补充说：尽管猎人声称狩猎能让野生动物种群保持平衡，但猎人的执照费实际上被用 来"操纵少数狩猎物种过度繁殖，代价是数量大得多的非狩猎物种，结果造成生物多样性、 遗传完整性和生态平衡的丧失"。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 It keeps game population under control. 说"让狩猎物种数量受控"，但 Kirk 恰恰指 出 license fees 是 manipulate a few game species into overpopulation——是制造 过度繁殖，而非控制数量。 B) 无中生有 It turns hunting into a sport of the rich. 说"把狩猎变成富人的运动"，原文从未提及 收费让狩猎变贵或仅富人可及。 C) ✓ 正确 resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance ↔ It leads to ecological imbalance. 预判"执照费导致生态失衡"完整对应 It leads to ecological imbalance.，且把原文三项 后果（diversity / integrity / balance）中最具概括性的 ecological balance 留作落 点，正是六级正确项的典型做法。 D) 与原文相反 It helps stop killing for pleasure. 说"有助于停止为娱乐而杀"，与 Kirk 全篇的批评立 场矛盾——他在 P2 上半段还指责 hunters kill for pleasure，根本不可能认为执照费能 解决这件事。 美国人道协会反对狩猎的论点是什么? options.label: B

questions.stem: What is the argument of the Humane Society of the United States against hunting?

analysis.label: 判型

A) Overpopulation is not an issue for most hunted animals. B) Hunting deprives animal populations of their food sources. C) Many birds and small animals are being irrationally killed. D) Hunting is universally acknowledged as a savage behavior.

analysis.text: What is the argument of the Humane Society of the United States against hunting? 是 What is the N? 的判断句；against hunting 修饰 argument，意为"反对狩猎的论点"。 结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

analysis.text: According to the Humane Society of the United States, the vast majority of hunted species— such as waterfowl, rabbits, upland birds and mourning doves—"provide minimal nutrition and do not require population control." 美国人道协会指出：绝大多数被猎杀的物种——例如水禽、兔子、高地鸟和哀鸽——"营养 价值极低，且并不需要被控制数量"。

questions.stem: When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干 When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner? 用 when 索取一 个明确条件，原文必有 Varner 给出的判定标准。 54. When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner? A) When it benefits animals and their ecosystem. B) When it serves both human and animal interests. C) When it is indispensable to humans' subsistence. D) When it stabilizes the population of animal species.

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner? 是 when 引导的特殊 疑问句，morally justifiable 是"副词+形容词"作表语，意为"在道德上可被辩护的"。结构清 晰，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Hunting "designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both"—what Varner terms "therapeutic hunting"—is defensible, while subsistence and sport hunting—both of which only benefit human beings—are not. Varner 称那种"旨在保障目标物种整体福祉、其生态系统完整性、或二者兼顾"的狩猎为"治 疗性狩猎"，认为它是可被辩护的；而生计性狩猎和运动性狩猎——这两者只让人类得益 ——则不可辩护。

options.label: C

analysis.text: A) 以偏概全 Effective protection of animal habitats. 只截取末句 habitat destruction 的一个侧 面，而 green leaders 推动的核心是"双方合作"——栖息地保护只是合作理由，不是他 们倡导的概念。 B) 以偏概全 Strict control over urban development. 同样只截取 urban sprawl 一个侧面，且 green leaders 并未单独倡导"严控城市发展"，而是把"deplore urban sprawl"作为双方 合作的共同立场。 C) ✓ 正确 green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups ↔Coordinated efforts of hunters and environmentalists. 预判"猎人与环保派联手合作"与 Coordinated efforts of hunters and environmentalists. 一一对应，且选项的抽象度（concept）正好匹配题干 What concept 的提问层级。 D) 无中生有 A compromise between development and animal protection. 引入"发展 vs 动物保 护的妥协"二元对立，原文从未涉及"开发派 vs 保护派的妥协"。

options.label: D

matching.raw:
A) Until a few decades ago, scholars believed that young children know very little, if anything, about what others are thinking. Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget, who is credited with founding the scientific study of children's thinking, was convinced that preschool children cannot consider what goes on in the minds of others. The interviews and experiments he conducted with kids in the middle of the 20th century suggested that they were trapped in their subjective viewpoints, incapable of imagining what others think, feel or believe.
B) Much of the subsequent research on early childhood thinking was highly influenced by Piaget's ideas. Scholars sought to refine his theory and empirically confirm his views. But it became increasingly clear that Piaget seemed to have gravely underestimated the intellectual powers of very young kids before they can make themselves understood by speech. Researchers began to devise ever more ingenious ways of figuring out what goes on in the minds of babies, and the resulting picture of their abilities shows subtle variations. Consequently, the old view of children's egocentric(自我中心 的) nature and intellectual weaknesses has increasingly fallen out of favor and become replaced by a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds, even in the "youngest young."
C) Historically, children didn't receive much respect for their mental powers. Piaget not only believed that children were "egocentric" in the sense that they were unable to differentiate between their own viewpoint and that of others; he was also convinced that their thinking was characterized by systematic errors and confusions. When playing with others, they don't cooperate because they do not realize there are different roles and perspectives. He was convinced that children literally cannot "get their act together": instead of playing cooperatively and truly together, they play side by side, with little regard for others. And when speaking with others, a young child supposedly cannot consider the listener's viewpoint but "talks to himself without listening to others."
D) Piaget and his followers maintained that children go through something like a dark age of intellectual development before slowly and gradually becoming enlightened by reason and rationality as they reach school age. Alongside this enlightenment develops an ever growing understanding of other persons, including their attitudes and views of the world.
E) Today, a very different picture of children's mental development emerges. Psychologists continually reveal new insights into the depth of young children's knowledge of the world, including their understanding of other minds. Recent studies suggest that even infants are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs.
F) Part of the motivation to revise some of Piaget's conclusions stemmed from an ideological shift about the origin of human knowledge that occurred in the second half of the 20th century. It became increasingly unpopular to assume that a basic understanding of the world can be built entirely from experience. This was in part prompted by theorist Noam Chomsky, who argued that something as complex as the rules of grammar cannot be picked up from exposure to speech, but is supplied by an inborn "language faculty." Others followed suit and defined further "core areas" in which knowledge allegedly cannot be pieced together from experience but must be possessed at birth. One such area is our knowledge of others' minds. Some even argue that a basic knowledge of others' minds is not only possessed by human infants, but must be evolutionarily old and hence shared by our nearest living relatives, the great apes.
G) To prove that infants know more in this realm than had been acknowledged, researchers needed to come up with innovative ways of showing it. A big part of why we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities is the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal.
H) Instead of engaging babies in dialog or having them execute complex motor tasks, the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions. The idea of focusing on these "small behaviors" is that they give kids the chance to demonstrate their knowledge implicitly and spontaneously without having to respond to questions or instructions. For example, children might look longer at an event that they did not expect to happen, or they might show facial expressions indicating that they have sympathetic concern for others. When researchers measure these less demanding, and often involuntary, behaviors, they can detect a sensitivity to others' mental states at a much younger age than with the more taxing methods that Piaget and his followers deployed.
I) In the 1980s, these kinds of implicit measures became customary in developmental psychology. But it took a while longer before these tools were employed to measure children's grasp of the mental lives of others.
J) In a set of experiments, my colleagues at the University of Southern California and I found evidence that babies can even anticipate how others will feel when their expectations are disappointed. We acted out several puppet(木偶) shows in front of two-year-old children. In these puppet shows, a protagonist (Cookie Monster) left his precious belongings (cookies) on stage and later returned to fetch them. What the protagonist did not know was that an antagonist had come and messed with his possessions. The children had witnessed these acts and attentively watched the protagonist return. We recorded children's facial and bodily expressions. Children bit their lips, wrinkled their nose or wiggled(扭动) in their chair when the protagonist came back, as if they anticipated the bewilderment and disappointment he was about to experience. Importantly, children showed no such reactions and remained calm when the protagonist had seen the events himself and thus knew what to expect. Our study reveals that by the tender age of two, kids not only track what others believe or expect; they can even foresee how others will feel when they discover reality.
K) Studies like this reveal that there is much more going on in small kids' and even infants' minds than was previously believed. With the explicit measures used by Piaget and successors, these deeper layers of kids' understanding cannot be accessed. The new investigative tools demonstrate that kids know more than they can say: when we scratch beneath the surface, we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of.
L) Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking, it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene because the original methods revealed essential facts about how children think that the new methods cannot uncover.
M) There's no consensus in today's science community about how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture. These behaviors clearly indicate a curiosity about what goes on in the mind of others, and probably a set of early intuitions coupled with a willingness to learn more. They pave the way to richer and more explicit forms of understanding of the minds of others. But they can in no way replace the child's growing ability to articulate and refine her understanding of how people behave and why.

One such area is our knowledge of others' minds. Some even argue that a basic knowledge of others' minds is not only possessed by human infants, but must be evolutionarily old and hence shared by our nearest living relatives, the great apes.

blocks.label: G
blocks.text: To prove that infants know more in this realm than had been acknowledged, researchers needed to come up with innovative ways of showing it. A big part of why we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities is the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal.

blocks.label: H
blocks.text: Instead of engaging babies in dialog or having them execute complex motor tasks, the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions. The idea of focusing on these "small behaviors" is that they give kids the chance to demonstrate their knowledge implicitly and spontaneously without having to respond to questions or instructions. For example, children might look longer at an event that they did not expect to happen, or they might show facial expressions indicating that they have sympathetic concern for others. When researchers measure these less demanding, and often involuntary, behaviors, they can detect a sensitivity to others' mental states at a much younger age than with the more taxing methods that Piaget and his followers deployed.

blocks.label: I
blocks.text: In the 1980s, these kinds of implicit measures became customary in developmental psychology. But it took a while longer before these tools were employed to measure children's grasp of the mental lives of others.

blocks.label: J
blocks.text: In a set of experiments, my colleagues at the University of Southern California and I found evidence that babies can even anticipate how others will feel when their expectations are disappointed. We acted out several puppet(木偶) shows in front of two-year-old children. In these puppet shows, a protagonist (Cookie Monster) left his precious belongings (cookies) on stage and later returned to fetch them. What the protagonist did not know was that an antagonist had come and messed with his possessions. The children had witnessed these acts and attentively watched the protagonist return. We recorded children's facial and bodily expressions. Children bit their lips, wrinkled their nose or wiggled(扭动) in their chair when the protagonist came back, as if they anticipated the bewilderment and disappointment he was about to experience. Importantly, children showed no such reactions and remained calm when the protagonist had seen the events himself and thus knew what to expect. Our study reveals that by the tender age of two, kids not only track what others believe or expect; they can even foresee how others will feel when they discover reality.

blocks.label: K
blocks.text: Studies like this reveal that there is much more going on in small kids' and even infants' minds than was previously believed. With the explicit measures used by Piaget and successors, these deeper layers of kids' understanding cannot be accessed. The new investigative tools demonstrate that kids know more than they can say: when we scratch beneath the surface, we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of.

blocks.label: L
blocks.text: Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking, it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene because the original methods revealed essential facts about how children think that the new methods cannot uncover.

blocks.label: M
blocks.text: There's no consensus in today's science community about how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture. These behaviors clearly indicate a curiosity about what goes on in the mind of others, and probably a set of early intuitions coupled with a willingness to learn more. They pave the way to richer and more explicit forms of understanding of the minds of others. But they can in no way replace the child's growing ability to articulate and refine her understanding of how people behave and why.

P1 People often discuss the dangers of too much stress, but lately a very different view of stress is gaining popularity: this view of stress, held by members of the positive stress movement, argues that stress might actually be beneficial. The positive stress movement is made up of people such as Zachary Rapp who are looking for an edge in a competitive world, and Rapp's routine is a good example of followers of the movement. He wakes up most mornings at dawn, goes for a run, sips black coffee while ripping through emails, and then steps into a freezing cold shower. This is a routine designed to reduce the stress of running simultaneously three different health and biotechnology companies for 18 hours a day.

P2 Although Rapp's practices may sound extreme, he is part of a growing movement, consisting largely of tech industry workers who claim that such radical tactics will help them live better and longer. Inspired by influential figures in different fields, including entertainers, athletes, entrepreneurs and scientists, positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort.

P3 Rapp argues that positive stress keeps him balanced. In addition to running and freezing showers, Rapp uses ice baths, hot yoga, and unconventional eating practices such as eliminating dairy, sugar, alcohol and various other foods high in carbohydrates. He believes that these practices, which put stress on his body, actually make him feel less stress from work. However, Rapp does not credit anyone in particular for his choices: he said he started using these methods in college, where he got into the habit of taking ice baths to recover from sports. He got back into it while trying to get his three companies off the ground.

P4 Rapp works long hours and sleeps only five to seven hours a night but he said he only gets sick once a year. For him, the difference between day-to-day stress, like the kind we feel when moving apartments, and positive stress is that the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance.

P5 One thought leader in the positive stress world is Dutch extreme athlete Wim Hof, who earned the name "ice man" for his ability to withstand severe cold using deep breathing exercises. Hof's ideas have become popular among tech industry elites and, thanks to Hof, cold showers are now a trend; indeed, some even call it a form of therapy.

P6 But it is important to note that not everyone agrees with these practitioners; indeed, some medical professionals argue that positive stress is not for everyone, and that it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older.

P1 Is hunting good or bad for the environment? Like so many hot button issues, the answer to this question depends upon who you ask. On the one hand, some say, nothing could be more natural than hunting, and indeed just about every animal species—including humans—has been either predator or prey at some point in its evolution. And, ironic as it sounds, since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now reproduce beyond the environment's carrying capacity.

P2 On the other hand, many environmental and animal advocates see hunting as savage, arguing that it is morally wrong to kill animals, regardless of practical considerations. According to Glenn Kirk of the California-based The Animals' Voice, hunting "causes immense suffering to individual wild animals…" and is "irrationally cruel because unlike natural predation(捕食), hunters kill for pleasure …" He adds that, despite hunters' claims that hunting keeps wildlife populations in balance, hunters' license fees are used to "manipulate a few game species into overpopulation at the expense of a much larger number of non-game species, resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance."

P3 Beyond moral issues, others contend that hunting is not practical. According to the Humane Society of the United States, the vast majority of hunted species—such as waterfowl, rabbits, upland birds and mourning doves—"provide minimal nutrition and do not require population control."

P4 Author Gary E. Varner suggests in his book, In Nature's Interests, that some types of hunting may be morally justifiable while others may not be. Hunting "designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both"—what Varner terms "therapeutic hunting"— is defensible, while subsistence and sport hunting—both of which only benefit human beings—are not.

P5 Regardless of one's individual stance, fewer Americans hunt today than in recent history. Data gathered by the U. S. Fish & Wildlife Service in 2006 show that only five percent of Americans—some 12.5 million individuals—consider themselves hunters today, down from nine percent in 2001 and 15 percent in 1996.

P6 Public support for hunting, however, is on the rise. A 2007 survey by Responsive Management Inc. found that eighty percent of respondents agreed that "hunting has a legitimate place in modern society," and the percentage of Americans indicating disapproval of hunting declined from 22 percent in 1995 to 16 percent in 2007.

P7 Perhaps matching the trend among the public, green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups: After all, both deplore urban sprawl and habitat destruction.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying " The best preparation for tomorrow is doing your best today. " You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: The saying "The best preparation for tomorrow is doing your best today" reminds us of a simple yet profound truth: our future is not built by anxious planning alone, but by the concrete effort we invest at this very moment. In my view, giving our best today is precisely how we lay a solid foundation for a brighter tomorrow. This idea holds true in almost every field. Take exam preparation as an example. A student who reviews a little every day, solving problems and memorizing words, gradually accumulates the knowledge that pays off on the test day. In contrast, those who indulge in procrastination and cram at the last minute often panic and fail. The same logic applies to career growth: the skills we sharpen through daily practice quietly prepare us for opportunities we cannot yet foresee. Therefore, instead of worrying about an uncertain future, we should seize the day and focus on what we can control right now. If each of us does our best today, tomorrow will take care of itself. The most reliable preparation is always the honest effort we make in the present.

sentences.text: 小说是公认杰作（主语策略：原句主语） 判断句，主语 The Romance of the Three Kingdoms（沿用统一译名）或代词 It，系动词 is，表 语 an acknowledged literary masterpiece。依据 《三国演义》是一部公认的文学杰作。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 简单判断句无需降级 本句仅一个判断动作，"公认的"作前置形容词 acknowledged / recognized 修饰 masterpiece 即 可，无其余分句需降级。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 客观评价，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 is。 冠词 "一部杰作"泛指，用不定冠词；因 acknowledged 以元音音 /ə/ 开头，须用 an：an acknowledged literary masterpiece。 用词 "公认的"用 acknowledged / widely recognized；"杰作"用 masterpiece，比 great work 更精 准地道。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Romance of the Three Kingdoms is an acknowledged literary masterpiece. 6. 自面世以来，这部小说不断吸引着一代又一代的读者，并且对中国文化产生了广泛而持久的 影响 。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 小说吸引读者并产生影响（主语策略：原句主语） 主语"这部小说"用 the novel；"并且"连接两个并列谓语，主干为 the novel has attracted … readers and (has) had … influence，两动作共用主语。依据 这部小说不断吸引着一代又一代的读 者，并且对中国文化产生了广泛而持久的影响。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 时间状语前置并列谓语收尾 "自面世以来"是时间状语，前置为 Since its publication / first appearance；"一代又一代的读 者"译 generations of readers 作宾语；"广泛而持久的"作前置形容词 wide and lasting 修饰 influence；"对中国文化"用介词短语 on Chinese culture 收尾。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "自面世以来…不断…"是从过去持续到现在的动作，由 Since 触发现在完成时：has attracted、 has had（或 has exerted），不可用一般过去时。 主谓一致 主语 the novel 第三人称单数，完成时助动词用 has。 单复数 "一代又一代"用复数 generations of readers，readers 复数。 介词搭配 "对…产生影响"用 have/exert an influence on，"对中国文化"的"对"用 on，不用 to/for。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Since its first appearance, the novel has continuously attracted generations of readers and has exerted a wide and lasting influence on Chinese culture. 英语六级 2020年7月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
